# PRACTIQ: A Practical Conversational Text-to-SQL dataset with Ambiguous and Unanswerable Queries

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#practiq)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/2025.naacl-long.13.pdf) · NAACL 2025 proceedings, pages 255-273

**Reading coverage:** All nineteen PDF pages, Sections 1-6, limitations and Appendices A-G, full construction prompts, examples, annotation instructions and result tables; figure captions and main reported results covered.

## Research question

Conventional SQL benchmarks omit requests needing clarification, missing data or a change to the requested task.

## Method

PRACTIQ mutates Spider schemas/values or questions into four ambiguous and four unanswerable types. It constructs final SQL first, then reverse-generates clarification replies, with executable-output filtering and LLM quality checks. Some ambiguity types also receive all-options SQL.

## Evaluation

Few-shot baselines perform nine-way question classification and DIN-SQL generation after receiving the supplied clarification exchange. Classification compares lexical retrieval with oracle cell values. Human review samples question labels and 90 conversations rather than validating every generated dialogue.

## What the results support

Fine-grained classification and post-clarification SQL remain difficult. Missing-information examples often recover by changing the requested attribute/entity, not by discovering information that answers the original request.

## Limits and qualifications

The user is scripted backward from target SQL; the evaluation does not measure agent-led dialogue or repair of imperfect replies. Nonexistent filter values are labeled unanswerable by benchmark convention, which must be distinguished from valid empty/zero results. Printed category counts and aggregate totals disagree.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Useful for category-specific diagnosis and clarification incorporation with explicit construction and answerability conventions.

## Checks against the paper

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.

| Missing filter values make all such SQL requests unanswerable. | Table 2 and Appendix E.5 define this operational category and replace the missing value in follow-up. | Table 2; Appendix E.5 | Preserve benchmark semantics; do not generalize to rejecting every valid empty result. |
